video_goal: Demonstrate how to accurately test soil pH using the Luster Leaf Rapitest 1605 digital tester.
required_subjects_and_props: Luster Leaf Rapitest 1605 digital tester, cup of dry soil, bottle of distilled water, spoon, cleaning pad, paper towel

outline_steps.visual_action: Hands place the green Luster Leaf Rapitest 1605 tester, a plastic cup containing dry soil, and a bottle of distilled water onto a flat work surface.
Fingers firmly rub the included abrasive cleaning pad up and down the metal probe of the Rapitest 1605 to remove oxidation.
A hand tips the bottle of distilled water, pouring a steady stream into the cup of dry soil until the soil is fully saturated.
A metal spoon vigorously stirs the soil and distilled water mixture, breaking up dry lumps to create a thick, muddy slurry.
A thumb presses the power button on the front of the Rapitest 1605, causing the digital screen to illuminate with a default number.
A hand grips the green plastic housing of the tester and pushes the metal probe straight down into the center of the mud slurry.
The hand twists the tester back and forth slightly in the mud to pack the wet soil tightly against the metal probe.
The camera focuses entirely on the digital screen of the Rapitest 1605 as the numbers rapidly fluctuate up and down.
The fluctuating numbers on the digital screen slow down and finally lock onto a stable reading of '6.5'.
The hand pulls the tester straight up, extracting the muddy metal probe from the soil cup.
A white paper towel wraps around the metal probe and wipes downward, removing all the wet mud and leaving the metal shiny.
The thumb presses the power button on the Rapitest 1605 one last time, and the digital screen goes blank.
